message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season, which can occur year‑round but peaks in spring and summer. A male will approach a receptive female, often after establishing dominance over other males. He may scent‑mark or roar to attract her. Once she signals readiness (by emitting a low growl or vocalizing), the male mounts her from behind, positioning his front legs on her shoulders. The mating lasts only a few seconds—typically 5–10 minutes—after which the male leaves. Females may mate with multiple males, leading to paternity confusion that benefits cub survival.
